applicability: Any 'a percent OF b'. The identity a% of b = b% of a is exact for every pair of real numbers a and b, because a% of b = (a/100)*b = (a*b)/100 = (b/100)*a = b% of a - multiplication commutes, and dividing by 100 is the same step on both sides. So the swap is always allowed and never approximate; the only question is which of the two forms is easier to do in your head, and you pick that one. It applies to a plain proportion ('percent of'), which includes 'what is the VAT part', 'what is the tip', 'how much is the discount worth'. It does NOT apply to a percent CHANGE - 'a% off b', 'a% added to b' - because those subtract or add the proportion from b, and b - a*b/100 is not symmetric in a and b.
carry_case: Percent OFF, where the same swap is false. With the drawn numbers: 88% OFF 75 leaves 75 - 66 = 9, while 75% OFF 88 leaves 88 - 66 = 22. The removed part is the same 66 in both, but what is left is not, so a% off b = b% off a fails for every pair with a != b - the equality b - a*b/100 = a - a*b/100 forces a = b. The 'of' form has no exception at all; the exception is over-extending it to the 'off' form.

steps.working: a% of b = b% of a

draws.operand: b (the quantity the percent is taken of)
draws.seed_note: assigned seed + 1, declared before the draw, because two operands come from two different declared ranges and one stream cannot serve both

operand_draw.declared_mapping_rationale: Both mappings are presentational only. The identity is exact for every real a and b, so no drawn value could ever have been rejected on mathematical grounds and the rejection rate is 0 on both streams. The ranges are chosen so the card carries whole numbers: a is a multiple of 4 in 12..96 and b is in {25, 50, 75}, hence a*b/100 is always an integer. Nothing in either range determines whether the trick works - only how the answer renders.

range_revisions.declared: a and b both integer 11..99, single stream, seed 343064731, n=2
range_revisions.discarded_because: The method is about swapping to the easier side. With two arbitrary two-digit numbers neither side is easier (91% of 34 vs 34% of 91), so the range could not carry the lesson. Range replaced, draw never re-rolled.

75% of 91 = 68.25 - correct but it puts a decimal on the card for no teaching gain. The a-range was replaced with multiples of 4 so the swapped side lands on a whole number. Again a range change, not a re-roll.
